drafted.title: Insufficient validation of agent tool and model-serving input parameters
drafted.description: An agent framework, MCP server, orchestration tool, or model-serving endpoint accepts tool-call arguments, file paths, headers, or inference parameters without checking type, range, structure, or allowed values before acting on them, letting an attacker supply crafted values that trigger command/code injection, path traversal, authentication or allowlist bypass, or crashes. Because agents chain untrusted LLM output and external data directly into tool invocations and model-serving calls, a single unvalidated parameter can escalate to remote code execution or denial of service across the whole pipeline.

drafted.title: XML external entity injection via unhardened parser on tool-ingested documents
drafted.description: An agent tool or dependency parses attacker-influenced XML (uploaded documents, SOAP/SAML messages, config/import files, webhook payloads) with DTD processing and external entity resolution left enabled, letting the attacker declare external entities that make the parser read local files, perform SSRF against internal/cloud-metadata endpoints, or exhaust resources via entity expansion. Because agents routinely pipe untrusted content from users, connectors, or other agents into document/parsing tools, a single unhardened XML parser anywhere in the tool-calling or ingestion chain becomes a direct path to data exfiltration or internal network pivoting.

drafted.title: Downstream injection via unsanitized LLM/tool-generated commands, queries, or templates
drafted.description: An agent or MCP tool forwards LLM-generated or attacker-influenced content (shell arguments, SQL/Cypher/LDAP queries, Jinja/SSTI templates, YAML/Kubernetes manifests, log lines, or environment variables) to a downstream interpreter without neutralizing special syntax elements, letting an attacker who controls any upstream input — a prompt, crawled web page, tool response, or filename — smuggle interpreter-level metacharacters that execute arbitrary commands, queries, or code in the agent's execution environment. Because agents chain many heterogeneous backends (databases, container runtimes, template engines, CI runners) behind a single natural-language-driven decision loop, this generic neutralization failure recurs across virtually every tool integration and typically yields full remote code execution.

drafted.title: Token and credential theft via unvalidated redirect URI in agent auth flows
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent service (OAuth/SSO endpoint, MCP registry client registration, login/logout handler) accepts an attacker-supplied URL in a redirect/callback parameter without validating it against an allow-list of trusted origins, then forwards the user's browser or the agent's HTTP client to that URL after completing authentication. This lets an attacker exfiltrate authorization codes, session tokens, or credentials and stage convincing phishing pages within a delegated-authorization flow the agent or its users trust.

drafted.title: Path traversal in agent file/model/artifact handling endpoints
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent service (e.g. model server, webui, log viewer, archive extractor) accepts attacker-controlled filenames or path parameters without normalizing or restricting them, allowing '../' or absolute-path sequences to escape the intended directory. This lets attackers read arbitrary files (credentials, config, memory stores), overwrite application files, or plant executable payloads (e.g. via extension install, settings apply, or tar/zip extraction) leading to full remote code execution.

drafted.title: Cross-origin tool invocation via missing Origin/Host header validation on MCP transport
drafted.description: An MCP server's HTTP/SSE transport accepts requests without validating the Origin or Host header, so a malicious web page rendered in a victim's browser (directly, or via DNS rebinding to reach a loopback-bound server) can send cross-origin requests the server treats as trusted, invoking tools, reading resources, or exfiltrating data. This defeats the browser's same-origin isolation guarantee and turns any visited website into a vector for unauthenticated control of the agent's privileged tool surface.

drafted.title: Arbitrary code execution via eval injection in agent code-execution tools and expression evaluators
drafted.description: Agent frameworks and orchestration platforms (e.g. LangChain, Flowise, Langflow, n8n, MindsDB, Agno, Xinference) frequently pass LLM tool-call output, user-supplied workflow expressions, or custom-node code directly into Python/JS eval()/exec() without sandboxing or input validation. An attacker who controls a prompt, tool argument, workflow config, or model response can inject code that the evaluator executes with the host process's full privileges, achieving remote code execution on the agent's runtime.

drafted.title: Arbitrary file read/write via relative path traversal in tool filename parameters
drafted.description: An agent-exposed tool or endpoint (file upload, workflow save/load, profile picture, personality/plugin folder, batch delete, etc.) accepts a user- or model-controlled filename/path argument and concatenates it onto a base directory without canonicalizing or validating it, so sequences like '../' or absolute/symlinked paths let an attacker escape the intended storage directory. Because the agent or its backing service executes these file operations with its own privileges, the result is arbitrary file read, overwrite, or creation on the host, which can leak secrets, corrupt application state, or achieve remote code execution when the written file is later loaded or executed.

drafted.title: Unrestricted upload of dangerous file types enabling remote code execution
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent service exposes a file upload path (chat attachments, knowledge-base ingestion, plugin/config install, media gallery) that fails to properly validate the uploaded file's type, extension, or content against what the server will later interpret or execute, letting an attacker disguise a web shell, script, or executable config as an allowed file and achieve arbitrary code execution on the host running the agent. Because agent platforms often grant the upload-handling component broad filesystem and process privileges, this single missing check routinely escalates straight to full host compromise rather than mere data exposure.

drafted.title: Prototype pollution in agent tool dependencies enabling RCE
drafted.description: An attacker supplies crafted keys (e.g. __proto__, constructor.prototype) through ordinary-looking input — JSON bodies, form data, glob patterns, template strings, or config merges — to a library embedded in an agent's tool, workflow engine, or MCP server that recursively assigns object properties without blocking dunder keys, corrupting the shared Object.prototype for the whole process. Because many agent frameworks reuse the now-polluted prototype for validation, templating, or dynamic code paths, this single injection can cascade into auth/validation bypass, sandbox escape, or full remote code execution across otherwise-unrelated tool calls.
